mobile_tools.name: trace_native_ui_action
mobile_tools.description: Trace one unique compiled UI action, object ID, native symbol or exact function address through authored connections, encoded or symbolized Objective-C handlers, and bounded static call references. Typed direct and resolved indirect calls, ambiguous candidates, inferred untyped provider callees, and targetless sites remain distinct. Runtime reachability is unknown; use trace_native_values for recovered value dependencies.

mobile_tools.name: observe_native_ui
mobile_tools.description: Observe an already-running native app by PID and window ID, bound to the active Mach-O target. Captures a bounded accessibility tree and selected-window screenshot; OS permission denial fails without broad capture or target launch. native_ui_deadline_ms is the observation deadline (omitted means 180000 ms, range 1..2147483647, next call). It does not raise the fixed 67108864-byte output allowance or the 180000 ms wait-step cap.

mobile_tools.name: capture_native_ui_scenario
mobile_tools.description: Run selected-element press, increment/decrement scroll, AXValue text entry and bounded wait steps in one exact native app window. Returns ordered before/after captures and action/capture failures. Actions can change app data, network activity and persistent state; application state is left as-is and restoration is not attempted. native_ui_deadline_ms is the scenario deadline (omitted means 180000 ms, range 1..2147483647, next call). It does not raise the fixed 67108864-byte output allowance or the 180000 ms wait-step cap.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_android_package
mobile_tools.description: Inspect a local APK's package, SDK and permission declarations, decoded manifest and class/resource counts, with a bounded static component projection. Omitted or complete detail preserves the complete result. Select detail: "summary" for all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text or duplicate raw calls; retains the complete source and returns a distinct linked inspect_analysis_view summary. Read the exact retained manifest with view kind android, facet manifest, offset and limit (UTF-16 code units), using normalized_result.parent_evidence_id. Does not execute the APK or verify signatures. Requires a caller-supplied JADX MCP JAR and JDK; uses one worker in an isolated temporary workspace.

mobile_tools.name: search_android_classes
mobile_tools.description: Search complete top-level decompiler class-name rows in an explicit local APK by case-sensitive substring. Empty query inventories all rows. Repeated names remain repeated and appear in duplicate_names; the provider accepts only class names for lookup, so these rows do not identify which same-name class node a later lookup selects. Retains artifact and engine identity; no APK execution.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_android_class
mobile_tools.description: Inspect one exact Android class's parsed methods, fields and inner classes, including synthetic members. Returns display signatures, exact DEX prototypes and encoded static final field values without generating source. A prototype is not a complete raw method ID; overload indices remain consistent within the artifact and engine session.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_android_method
mobile_tools.description: Decompile one Android method with smali fallback. Requires explicit overload_index when multiple methods share a name. Reports its DEX prototype, representation, fallback markers and source truncation; display signatures may be aliases.

mobile_tools.name: trace_android_references
mobile_tools.description: Trace incoming static using nodes to an exact Android class or selected method overload. The total counts containing nodes, not individual invoke instructions. Use inspect_android_class to choose an overload_index when names collide. Source lines and the containing node dex_offset remain unknown. direct_invokes carries exact DEX code-unit instruction offsets when available; direct_invokes_exhaustive false marks byte-bounded partial instruction evidence, and null means coverage is unknown. Using-node coverage remains separate; no runtime calls are inferred.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_adb_client
mobile_tools.description: Inspect the caller-selected adb client: resolved binary, version, and install path. Never contacts devices and never starts the adb server. REA never installs platform tools; select a binary with REA_ADB_PATH (absolute) or adb on PATH.

mobile_tools.name: list_adb_devices
mobile_tools.description: List attached devices exactly as `adb devices -l` reports them: serial, state, transport, model metadata, and an inferred emulator/physical kind with its evidence basis. Emulators and USB or network devices appear alike; REA neither starts nor manages them. May start the local adb server on first use.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_adb_device
mobile_tools.description: Inspect one device's build identity through a fixed `getprop` whitelist: Android and SDK versions, security patch, fingerprint, product identity, CPU ABIs, and debuggable flag, plus the observed emulator indicator ro.kernel.qemu. Present properties retain empty values; omitted keys were not reported. Read-only with respect to the device.

mobile_tools.name: list_adb_packages
mobile_tools.description: List installed packages on one device with each base APK's device path, optionally scoped to third-party or system packages. Paths are device filesystem paths, not host-local. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: pull_adb_package
mobile_tools.description: Pull one installed package's complete APK set (base plus every split, as `pm path` reports) from the device into a caller-selected output directory, creating a package-named subdirectory that must not already exist. Every pulled file is digested with SHA-256; partial pulls keep successful artifacts and per-file failure reasons. The device keeps the originals.

mobile_tools.name: read_adb_logcat
mobile_tools.description: Read a bounded dump of the device log (`logcat -d -t`) for one buffer, optionally restricted to a process id. No streaming, no clearing; the newest lines are kept when the count cap trims. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_adb_package
mobile_tools.description: Inspect installed-package versions, install times, installer, user id, flags, and requested-permission count through read-only `dumpsys package`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in bounded numeric_issues and make coverage partial; version_code stays exact text. Unknown sections are not inferred.

mobile_tools.name: pull_adb_file
mobile_tools.description: Pull one absolute device path (a database, shared-preferences XML, or any readable file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it with SHA-256. The local copy must not already exist. Read-only with respect to the device.

mobile_tools.name: push_adb_file
mobile_tools.description: Push one local file to an absolute device path. If the destination is an existing directory, adb places the file inside it under the local basename and the result reports that file path. A device-mutating tool: checks for an existing destination file before transfer and refuses it unless overwrite is explicitly requested; this check is not atomic and another process can create the path before adb writes. The private staged copy remains non-writable and preserves source executable bits. When the device provides sha256sum, the transfer is verified by comparing it with the local digest.

mobile_tools.name: capture_adb_screen
mobile_tools.description: Capture one frame of the device screen as a PNG (`screencap -p` through exec-out, no device-side file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it and reporting its dimensions. No recording or interaction.

mobile_tools.name: list_adb_processes
mobile_tools.description: List running processes exactly as `ps -A` reports them: user, pid, ppid, rss, state, and name. Useful for pairing with instrumentation lanes. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: list_adb_directory
mobile_tools.description: List the immediate children of one absolute device directory, including hidden entries: names, kinds, permissions, owner, group, sizes, dates, and symlink targets. Names and targets preserve embedded newlines. Recognizes the standard errors for absent paths and denied reads. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: list_adb_features
mobile_tools.description: List the device's declared hardware and software features (`pm list features`) for device fingerprinting. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: list_adb_services
mobile_tools.description: List the device's binder services with their interfaces (`service list`). Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_adb_display
mobile_tools.description: Read physical and override size/density from `wm size` and `wm density`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in numeric_issues with partial coverage; optional values remain null. Required physical-size failures retain partial display facts. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: inspect_adb_window
mobile_tools.description: Report the window manager's focus declarations with display context, original lines and explicit summary status. Reads `dumpsys window windows`, falling back to `displays` only when no focus field is declared. Singular fields are unknown for multiple contexts or repeated declarations; inspect focus_contexts for every observation. Read-only; no interaction occurs.

mobile_tools.name: read_adb_setting
mobile_tools.description: Read one settings value (`settings get`) from the system, secure, or global namespace. Absent keys report the device's own null observation. Read-only; writing settings is not exposed.

mobile_tools.name: collect_adb_bugreport
mobile_tools.description: Collect one device-generated bugreport archive (`adb bugreport`) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting the zip. The archive contains the device's own dumpstate, dumpsys, and logcat report; collection can take minutes. Read-only with respect to configuration.

mobile_tools.name: resolve_adb_packages
mobile_tools.description: Find installed packages by case-insensitive substring of the package name (e.g. `whatsapp` → `com.whatsapp`), returning each match's base APK device path. The first step of an easy get: resolve, then pull_adb_package the exact name. Read-only.

mobile_tools.name: install_adb_package
mobile_tools.description: Install one local APK on the device (`adb install [-r]`), recording the APK's host digest and byte size. A device-mutating tool: `replace_requested` records whether `-r` was selected; `replaced` is null because install success does not establish prior package state. The device's own Success/Failure verdict is preserved with its reason.

mobile_tools.name: uninstall_adb_package
mobile_tools.description: Request package removal for user 0 (`adb shell pm uninstall --user 0`) without data retention. A device-mutating tool; absent packages report the device's own refusal reason.

mobile_tools.name: start_adb_app
mobile_tools.description: Start one installed app's resolved launcher activity with `am start -W -n`. A device-mutating tool for dynamic analysis. The full wait report determines success; failures retain launch-attempt facts and raw output. Pair with `read_adb_logcat` (pid filter) and `list_adb_processes` to observe the app, and `stop_adb_app` to end the run.

mobile_tools.name: start_adb_activity
mobile_tools.description: Start an intent with `am start -W`: one action, optional data URI, optional explicit component, and up to 16 typed extras (string, boolean, int, long, float). A device-mutating tool; the full wait report determines success, with failed-attempt facts and raw output retained.

mobile_tools.name: stop_adb_app
mobile_tools.description: Force-stop every process of one package (`am force-stop`), ending a dynamic-analysis run. A device-mutating tool; it succeeds whether or not the package had running processes.

mobile_tools.name: identify_flutter_build
mobile_tools.description: Identify a Flutter app's build facts by pure parsing: observed Dart snapshot hashes from lib/<abi>/libapp.so, per-ABI library digests, the engine library's GNU build-id, and any labeled Dart version or toolchain strings libflutter.so carries. Complete snapshot coverage currently expects two independent headers in the legacy split VM/isolate profile; unified and other layouts can yield partial build facts. The snapshot hash maps to a Dart SDK release through an external dataset; REA performs no lookup. No engine, no execution, no external tools.

mobile_tools.name: decode_android_resources
mobile_tools.description: Decode one local APK's resources with `apktool d --no-src` in a provider-owned workspace that is removed after projection: the readable AndroidManifest.xml, apktool.yml version and SDK facts, the app's string resources (default or selected locales, bounded to 2000 entries per table), selectable string locales, and the decoded file count. The target APK is digest with SHA-256 before decoding; smali is skipped because Java-source recovery belongs to the JADX family. Optional decode_timeout_ms is the decode wall clock in milliseconds (default 600000, range 1..2147483647); omitted means 600000 and the value applies on the next decode. It does not raise the fixed output capture allowance or the version probe.

mobile_tools.name: project_android_application_graph
mobile_tools.description: Project authenticated APK inventory_artifact Evidence into an execution-free Android application inventory. Reports exact component paths and hashes, runtime-family hints, and path-based bridge hypotheses without decoding DEX, executing the APK, or claiming observed runtime calls.
